title: The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures
subtitle: An ancestor takes the defence
summary: The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures is Capcom's courtroom adventure following Ryunosuke Naruhodo, an ancestor of Phoenix Wright, between Japan and Britain around the turn of the twentieth century. Accompanied by judicial assistant Susato Mikotoba, he encounters unfamiliar legal customs and the detective Herlock Sholmes. Its original Nintendo 3DS release begins a connected historical mystery that later reached a worldwide audience through The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles. Investigations and trials remain the foundation, but the setting gives the young defence lawyer new institutions and assumptions to understand.
body: The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures is Capcom's courtroom adventure following Ryunosuke Naruhodo, an ancestor of Phoenix Wright, between Japan and Britain around the turn of the twentieth century. Accompanied by judicial assistant Susato Mikotoba, he encounters unfamiliar legal customs and the detective Herlock Sholmes. Its original Nintendo 3DS release begins a connected historical mystery that later reached a worldwide audience through The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles. Investigations and trials remain the foundation, but the setting gives the young defence lawyer new institutions and assumptions to understand.

During a Dance of Deduction, Sholmes develops an impressive explanation from observations that do not quite support his conclusion. Ryunosuke examines the scene and redirects the deduction by identifying the overlooked detail. The pleasure comes from following a line of reasoning closely enough to recognise where it has gone astray. Objects and people can be inspected from different angles, making observation part of the correction. Sholmes supplies the performance and momentum, while the player supplies the small changes that turn it into a sounder account of events.

British trials introduce jurors whose opinions can bring a hearing close to an early conclusion. Summation Examination allows Ryunosuke to question those reasons and compare statements that conflict with one another. A contradiction between jurors can reopen the argument and provide another chance for the defence. Witnesses may also testify in groups, reacting to what the others say. The courtroom becomes a place where several accounts must be read together, extending the familiar search for contradictions beyond a single speaker and a single item of evidence.
story_headings: Correct the detective without losing the clue
A jury must explain its verdict
